    Script 2 Report Regeneration-Command Header Plan

    Created: 2026-06-24 Status: Stages 1–5 complete — every exporter embeds the regeneration-command header and all reports were re-published against the corrected live DB. Remaining: Stage 6 audit dispositions — the bot-config, ensemble, baseline and regime groups are reviewed and closed; only the _LEGACY group is pending (frozen — a thesis-state review, not regeneration), owned by the thesis Script 2 plans (see Stage 6). Stage 7 (headers on the planner-input / stats markdown) is also still open. Scope: Every Script 2 report/plan exporter, the reports they produce, and a shared header helper.

    RC benchmark backfill — corrected (2026-06-25). The risk-constrained benchmark had been backfilled with the wrong ATR (the input high price used as ATR), giving a near-zero benchmark and alpha_rc ≈ return. That bug is fixed and the corrected backfill applied to the live DB: 15,177 sessions recomputed (errors 0, friction untouched), session 1500 now $1,162.69 (was $46.14), both consistency checks PASS (see docs/audit/20260624_RC_BENCHMARK_BACKFILL_WRONG_ATR_AUDIT.md). The live DB now holds the correct RC values, so any report reading alpha_rc / Orig α (RC) regenerates against correct data. The pre-RC backup (Appendix C) is still the date-finding reference for canonical reproduction, since the canonical reports predate any RC backfill.

    Second correction (2026-06-30). The risk-constrained benchmark was recomputed for a last_price valuation bug and every report was re-published from the corrected live DB. The current regeneration grid is regenerate_reports/20260630/as_of_dates.csv, which adds a regenerate column (set per report by the separate regenerate_reports/mark_regenerate.py so a row can be skipped without hardcoding paths in the regenerator); it supersedes the 20260626 grid.

    1. Objective

    Make every generated Script 2 Markdown report self-documenting: each report embeds, in its header (immediately after the existing provenance lines), the exact command and parameters needed to regenerate it from existing artifacts — including the historical DB cutoff --db-as-of-completed-at when one is required.

    Two outcomes:

    1. A validated date map: the exact --db-as-of-completed-at cutoff that reproduces each canonical report.
    2. Every exporter writes its own regeneration command into the report header, so any report can be rebuilt later with no plan archaeology.

    The work is staged so that nothing is modified until we have first proven, with the current reporters, that we can reproduce every canonical report byte-for-byte (except its generation timestamp).

    2. Non-Negotiable Rules

    • Stage 2 touches no script and no canonical artifact. It only runs the current reporters into a staging tree and compares.
    • Every regenerated report must equal its canonical counterpart exactly in all values; the only allowed difference is the generation-timestamp line(s).
    • All staging output lives under scripts/thesis/script_2_thesis/_tmp/<staging_root>/. Never under /tmp.
    • _LEGACY artifacts (*_LEGACY*, *_LEGACY_PRE_RC.md) are never read from or written over.
    • No DB mutation, no backtest reruns. Reports are rebuilt from existing DB rows and existing result artifacts only.
    • All code/comments/docs in English. Every touched Python file passes mypy --strict, ruff, pylint >= 9.5, Pyright. Markdown passes markdownlint-cli2.
    • Run everything inside .venv.

    4. DB Date-Filter Strategy

    Every report is regenerated against an explicit --db-as-of-completed-at cutoff equal to the DB state at the moment its canonical version was last produced, so rows added to the DB afterward do not leak into the reproduction. The cutoff filters trials.completed_at, backtest_sessions.completed_at, and trades.closed_at at the query layer.

    A repo-wide sweep (all archived plans, all .md, audits, logs, JSON sidecars) found no per-report date table written anywhere: the only explicit --db-as-of-completed-at values recorded are two accepted cutoffs plus a few rejected attempts, all inside plan documents, and the eight merge_inputs.json sidecars all record db_as_of_completed_at: null. The canonical reports' own Generated: / Last update: lines are not a usable cutoff source — they are the latest re-render time (these files were regenerated many times), not the historical snapshot the report reflects. Likewise the git commit time is not used.

    The reliable per-report date source is the _LEGACY counterpart's embedded timestamp — the frozen original snapshot moment. Cutoff candidate per report, in priority order:

    1. Documented accepted cutoff from a plan for that run-tag (the two below).
    2. The _LEGACY counterpart's embedded Last update / Generated at / Generated timestamp (extracted below).
    3. Plan B — probe: when no _LEGACY date exists (Section 2 / Section 11 annexes carry no date line) or the candidate does not reproduce, bisect the cutoff (seeded by a sibling generated in the same batch) until the diff closes.

    In every case the candidate is confirmed by regenerating and running git diff against the current canonical report: the only allowed difference is the generation-timestamp line. If anything else differs, the candidate is wrong and we move down the list or probe.

    5. Execution Stages and Tasks

    Master ordered checklist. Detailed mechanics live in the Header Format, Exporter Command Templates, Comparator Inventory and Verification sections below, plus Appendix A (report inventory + candidate dates) and Appendix B (deprecated audits). Each stage runs only on Manu's go-ahead; Stages 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 change code or canonical files, Stages 2 and 2B only run the current exporters into _tmp.

    Process Overview — the four ordered phases

    The whole effort runs in this strict order; each phase is gated on Manu's go-ahead and nothing in a later phase starts until the earlier one is green:

    1. Reproduce everything and prove it — Stage 2B. With the current, unmodified exporters and the pre-RC backup DB, regenerate every in-scope non-_LEGACY report into _tmp, mirroring the canonical folder tree. git diff + the per-family comparator on each file vs its canonical; log every verdict to _tmp/<root>/checks.log. Goal: prove our commands + confirmed cutoffs reproduce the canonicals exactly (only the accepted deltas). The backup DB is used here because the canonicals predate the RC backfill, so reproducing them exactly needs the pre-backfill data. No script change, no canonical touch. Stage 2B surfaced three renderers that read benchmark/metrics from frozen artifacts instead of the DB — fixed first in Stage 2C (a correctness fix), then re-reproduced.
    2. Add the regen-command header + emission date to the exporters — Stages 3–4. Only after Stage 2B/2C are green.
    3. Regenerate everything again — this time against the current live DB — Stage 5 (5.1). The modified exporters now embed the header; the live DB carries the RC backfill, so the corrected RC values land in the new outputs.
    4. Publish over the canonicals — Stage 5 (5.4). Only after the publish matrix is approved. _LEGACY is never touched.

    6. Header Format (confirmed)

    Existing provenance lines stay intact; the two date lines and the regenerate section are inserted right after them. Two dates always: As-of date (fixed, = the --as-of-date value, the data's temporal anchor) and Last regenerated (auto, rewritten each render). Example for results/best_per_fold_5runs.md:

    # Script 2 — Top-3 Trial Candidates per Model per Fold

- As-of date: `2026-04-14T14:18:55+00:00`
- Last regenerated: 2026-06-13 14:34 UTC
Tiers present: **A + B + C + D + E**  (No tier filter — all tiers included)
Source runs:
- `20260319_035820`
- ...

## How to Regenerate

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/thesis/script_2_thesis/exporters/script2_best_per_fold.py \
  --summary-csv scripts/thesis/script_2_thesis/results/20260319_035820/script2_experiment_ids.csv \
  ... \
  --db-path database/rainbow_trader.sqlite --top-n 3 --rank-by alpha_rc \
  --as-of-date 2026-04-14T14:18:55+00:00 \
  --output-md scripts/thesis/script_2_thesis/results/best_per_fold_5runs.md
```

---

    The --as-of-date feeds --db-as-of-completed-at where the script filters the DB by completion time; on the non-window renderers (extra / bot-config / ensemble) it only sets the As-of date header line. Section title ## How to Regenerate.

    A.9 Ensemble plan inputs — generate_ensemble_backtest_plan.py (plan.md)

    One plan.md per combo. Today there are 504 (only the 6 Phase-1 roots); the 2 Phase-3 cross_fold_transfer roots have plan.json per combo but no plan.md — they ran from a batch spec (batches/20260614_phase3_cross_fold_transfer_promise{,_rc}.json) via run_ensemble_backtest_batch.py, which writes plan.json but never rendered the markdown.

    The Phase-1 and Phase-3 plan.json files have identical keys (planner_mode, summary_csvs, source_run_tags, source_trial_ids, merge_rules, selection_policy, selected_compatibility_bucket, candidates, …) — everything plan.md shows. So plan.md is rendered from the existing plan.json via a small new mode reusing build_plan_markdown, giving a plan.md (with the regeneration-command header) for all 696 combos, including the 2 Phase-3 roots. We do not re-run the planner against the current DB (it could re-select different candidates now that the DB has drifted); rendering from the stored plan.json is the faithful path. No --db-as-of applies (no DB read). The new render-from-plan.json mode is a Phase-2 code addition to generate_ensemble_backtest_plan.py.

    Why Phase-3 lacks plan.md: the batch runner has two paths. The normal path runs generate_ensemble_backtest_plan.py as a subprocess per combo (writes both plan.md and plan.json, used by Phase-1). The fixed-trial path (run_ensemble_backtest_batch.py::write_fixed_trial_plan_json, used by the Phase-3 cross-fold transfer) writes a synthetic plan.json only and never renders plan.md. The synthetic plan.json stores every field plan.md needs except total_candidates_scanned and rank_pool_size — two header counts that are meaningless for fixed-trial executions (no scan/rank step), so the rendered Phase-3 plan.md shows them as N/A. Fix going forward: add the plan.md render to the fixed-trial path so the batch emits it directly. Validation note: rendering an existing Phase-1 plan.md from its plan.json will differ from the original on exactly those two count lines (not stored in plan.json); persisting the two counts into plan.json would close that gap for future runs.

    Appendix B — Audits Invalidated by Regeneration (DEPRECATED)

    Disposition status. These audits are reviewed and closed group by group; the decision for each group lives in the owning thesis Script 2 plan (Stage 6), not here. Done: the bot-config group (consolidated into AUDIT/BOT_CONFIG/20260629_SCRIPT2_BOT_CONFIG_CONSOLIDATED_AUDIT.md, predecessors under AUDIT/BOT_CONFIG/DEPRECATED/, numbers refreshed); the ensemble group (consolidated into AUDIT/ENSEMBLES/20260701_SCRIPT2_ENSEMBLE_LINE_CONSOLIDATED_AUDIT.md, predecessors under AUDIT/ENSEMBLES/DEPRECATED/); the baseline group (AUDIT/BASELINES/20260620_ALWAYS_LONG_BASELINE_EXECUTED_AUDIT.md, verified against the corrected DB and kept in place); the regime group (three reference/interpretation audits under AUDIT/REGIME/ — verified against the corrected DB and the 2026-06-30 regenerated diagnostic report, references repointed and one stale figure fixed, all kept in place). Pending: the older AUDIT/_LEGACY/ thesis-state audits. The _DEPRECATED-rename + replacement mechanism described next is one option; the bot-config and ensemble groups used consolidation, the baseline and regime groups a verified keep-in-place.

    Because the base reports/anexos are regenerated, every hand-written audit whose insights derive from them is now based on changed data. At the end of the regeneration, each such audit is:

    1. renamed to add _DEPRECATED to the filename;
    2. given an opening header block containing: a DEPRECATED banner, the reason (the values it interpreted were regenerated on this pass), and a link to its NEW hand-written replacement audit (rewritten from the regenerated real data). It may also reference the source report/anexo it was built on — already captured in the Built on column of B.1.

    Each DEPRECATED manual audit therefore gets a new hand-written replacement audit, written from the regenerated real data, and the deprecated file links forward to it. The final DEPRECATED-vs-KEEP decision per file is confirmed when its header is written. Reference/policy/methodology docs that do not depend on report values are kept (and only updated if a field/label actually changed).

    Appendix C — Stage 2 Iteration Log (backup DB)

    Every reproduction iteration runs against the pre-RC backup database/rainbow_trader_backup_20260625T031041Z.sqlite. The current DB cannot reproduce canonical values after the RC benchmark backfill, so it is not used for date-finding. Staging root: scripts/thesis/script_2_thesis/_tmp/regen_repro_check_20260624/UNO/<tag>/. Comparison = git diff --no-index <canonical> <staged>, read and classified by hand (not the legacy comparators, which were built for legacy→new column/format normalization and do not fit canonical→staged).

    A cutoff is always a date — never none. These families read the DB through a completion-time window, so a date is always required to match the canonical experiment/trial set. Candidate order per pack: A = date documented in the archived publish command (20520 §10 / 20601 §8.2) when one exists; B = the _LEGACY report's embedded Last update; C = manual probe/bisect (generate → diff → adjust → repeat) until experiments, trials and trial counts match.

    Acceptance: the experiments appear with their trials and the SAME trial counts, and every value/ranking/row matches. Accepted residual deltas (each confirmed with Manu): the two metadata header lines (Last update generation timestamp and DB path), the live-running snapshot block (Current Trial, Prog/Status), .500 aggregate trade display, and the new Always Long column. Blocking: any change to values, counts, ranking order, or table rows.
